hints: Look first at the two most diagnostic regions in IR, the broad absorption around 3300 cm-1 and the region around 1700 cm-1 for carbonyls.
Notice the very broad, strong dip centred near 3300 cm-1 but no strong sharp dip near 1700 to 1750 cm-1, so think which functional group gives O-H without C=O.
Compare the four structures for C=O groups and O-H groups, and pick the one that has alcohol O-H and C-O but no aldehyde, acid or ester carbonyl.
walkthrough:
**Read the big broad peak on the left**

Look at the left side of the spectrum. There is a very broad, strong absorption (low transmittance) centred around 3300 cm-1.

That shape is classic for an O-H stretch:
$$\text{O-H (alcohol) } \approx 3200-3600 \text{ cm}^{-1}, \text{ broad}$$

**Check for a carbonyl peak**

Now look around 1700 to 1750 cm-1 where C=O always gives a very strong, sharp peak. This spectrum is essentially flat there.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{C=O } \approx 1680-1750 \text{ cm}^{-1}, \text{ strong sharp}$$
No peak here means no ester, no carboxylic acid, no aldehyde and no ketone.

**Use the missing C=O to eliminate**

Option A is an ester $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$, option C is a carboxylic acid $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, option D is a hydroxy-aldehyde $\text{CH}_2(\text{OH})(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{CHO}$. All three must show C=O.

Since C=O is absent, A, C and D are all ruled out.

**Confirm the alcohol diol fits**

Option B is $\text{CH}_2(\text{OH})\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{OH}$, a diol with a C=C bond. It has O-H but no C=O.

This matches perfectly: broad O-H near 3300 cm-1, C-H stretches just below 3000 cm-1, and strong C-O stretches near 1000 to 1100 cm-1. So Y could be B.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ is ethyl ethanoate, an ester. It must show a strong sharp C=O stretch around 1735 cm-1 and has no O-H, so it cannot give the broad 3300 cm-1 O-H band seen.
options.B: Correct. $\text{CH}_2(\text{OH})\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{OH}$ has two alcohol O-H groups and no C=O group. That explains the broad O-H absorption near 3300 cm-1, the C-H peaks near 2900 cm-1, the C-O peaks near 1000 cm-1, and the absence of a carbonyl peak near 1700 cm-1.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is butanoic acid. It would show C=O near 1710 cm-1 and a very, very broad O-H that extends from about 2500 to 3300 cm-1. The spectrum lacks C=O and the O-H is centred higher, typical of an alcohol, not an acid.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_2(\text{OH})(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{CHO}$ contains both an alcohol O-H and an aldehyde C=O. Although the O-H could fit the broad band, the required aldehyde C=O peak around 1720 cm-1 plus aldehydic C-H near 2720 and 2820 cm-1 pattern is missing.
